newsitem.title: UK: International LPG stays strong on US, Euro demand.
newsitem.headline: International LPG stays strong on US, Euro demand.

text.p: International liquefied natural gas (LPG) prices continued unusually high this week with demand in the U.S. and Europe leading the market, dealers said.
"Prices in Europe are very high compared to what we expected, and also compared to what we feel they should be based on recent history", said a Scandinavian trader.

Propane was particularly strong. A 10,000 tonne cargo traded at $242 CIF Sweden this week, but was seen well below the market price. "It was a top-up off a 30,000 tonne cargo already going there, and the price was low as the seller saved as lot of money by making it a single-port sale," said a trader.
He said two mid-week trades of around 10,000 tonnes and 15,000 tonnes at $257 cif NWE were a more accurate reflection of the current market.

High crude prices were not seen influencing LPG. "There is normally a link to crude through naphtha as a substitute for LPG in the petrochemical sector," said a trader. "But propane has gone so high that it has decoupled from the crude and naphtha prices, so crude is not an influence at the moment".
"Strong gas oil can have an impact on propane prices as there is some substitution between these fuels, but it is fairly limited. Still, the sentiment is strong," he added.
Instead, demand from the U.S. was seen as the leading factor in European strength, with Algerian still moving transatlantic rather than arriving in NWE and pressuring prices there.
And loading disruptions after problems at Norway's Kaarstoe terminal earlier in the month are still seen by some as a factor, even though normal operations were swiftly restored.
Butane in NWE weakened slightly as demand from refineries for gasoline blending slipped. "The blending requirement has failed to take off, so there's not such a need for it," said a coaster trader.
A trade was seen at $242 a tonne CIF U.K. West Coast for 10,000 tonnes of butane "and nobody was willing to pay more," said the seller.
While propane coasters on a FOB basis are trading at parity to large CIF cargoes, butane coasters are some $30 a tonne below propane as blending demand remains poor, a dealer said.
Mediterranean trade was hampered by full storage in Lavera and in Italy as end-user demand fails to draw down stocks. "It's full everywhere and there's no domestic market," said a trader.
A small 4,000 tonne propane lot was sold into Lavera at $255 a tonne during the week, but most saw offers for large cargoes no higher than $250.
Butane in the Mediterranean traded at $245.50 CIF Lavera early in the week, but this was also seen at the top end of the range as demand weakened later.

The Middle East market was slow as traders await the latest Saudi Contract Price (CP) -- expected to be announced on Monday or Tuesday -- against which most LPG, especially in markets east of Suez, is traded.
"Nobody wants to buy or sell at the moment," a trader said. "Sellers are asking a premium of $10 over the CP, but at this level buyers prefer to wait for the October price to be announced."

Propane and butane premiums to the CP in the Middle East were discussed at identical levels. "They're moving together," said a trader. "It doesn't always happen, but that's the position at the moment".

East Asian demand was limited by the fact that inventories, especially in Japan, remain high. One trader pointed out that estimated Japanese stocks at the end of September stood at 3.2 million tonnes, out of a total capacity of 3.4 million. This compares with stocks of 3.1 million at end September 1995.

The high inventories are forcing buyer's ideas down, and opening a wide gap with sellers. "Sellers are asking CP +45 C+F Japan, while buyers will not come higher than CP +35 to +37," said one trader. He added that, as in the Middle East, propane and butane are discussed at identical premiums to the CP.

Chinese prices are rising, said a trader, but demand is for small volumes only. Traders estimate handling costs into China at around $50 a tonne for small deliveries, so buyers willing to pay CP +35 into Japan are looking for CP +85 for onward sale to China.
-- Sebastian Alison, London Newsroom +44 171 542 6412.
